Rules decide what trades.

A closer look at the mechanics described in the FloatSheets product overview and backend specification.

{01}

Community nominations.

The proposed listing process allows the community to nominate names. Eligibility depends on objective source coverage, underlying liquidity, and exchange-tier criteria; a nomination alone does not create a market.

{02}

Data coverage is the first gate.

At least three independent licensed sources are specified for an eligible name. Average daily volume and other liquidity thresholds are also required. The documents do not provide a single universal ADV threshold, so this preview does not invent one.

{03}

Every new name starts guarded.

Markets begin with lower leverage and tight capacity limits. Graduation to looser parameters requires an operating track record in areas such as uptime, band behavior, and volume.

{04}

A phased universe.

F1 targets 25 guarded Nasdaq and NYSE small-cap markets. F2 adds OTC and penny-stock tiers, corporate-action handling, and listing rules. Later expansion remains gated by insurance capacity and oracle reliability.

{05}

Your local nomination.

The dashboard saves the ticker, company name, exchange, source count, and rationale on this device. Nothing is transmitted to a listing committee, data provider, or blockchain.
